correctness.rationale: For the explicitly specified iid position redraws, the renewal first-passage Laplace transform gives the exact mean and coefficient-of-variation square. The decreasing-distance density admits a probability-mixture-of-uniforms representation with a positive mixing length of finite mean. An algebraically checked derivative identity reduces the sign to the expectation of a symmetric two-variable kernel; the strict inequalities S(x)>2 and R(x)>(3-x)/2 show that kernel is strictly negative at all positive arguments. Endpoint behavior follows by concavity and dominated Laplace limits. The included standard-library program compares independent derivative and kernel calculations in 300 mixtures and 24 interval/target instances; this is corroboration, not the infinite-class proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The older mean-first-passage result does not imply a global second-moment derivative sign; the optimal-rate universal coefficient of variation equals one only at a finite interior mean optimizer, whereas the theorem here states strictly decreasing coefficient of variation greater than one at all finite rates and converging to one at infinity. A more abstract renewal theorem might imply the specialization and remains an explicit residual risk.

originality.rationale: Méndez, Flaquer-Galmés and Campos (arXiv:2401.01125, Sec. VII.B) give the coefficient-of-variation formula and numerical evidence for monotonicity for a uniform reset interval containing its target. The present result establishes strict monotonicity analytically, also for an off-center target, and for the broader class of all bounded decreasing reset-distance densities. Evans and Majumdar provide the distributed-reset first-moment framework; Reuveni gives a universal coefficient-of-variation value at a mean-optimal rate, not the all-rate monotonicity classification. Other general renewal fluctuation theorems remain a possible priority risk.
residual_risks: A broader renewal or Laplace-transform shape theorem may imply this sufficient condition without using the present kernel proof.
The priority assessment is based on checked relevant sources, not a census of all publications; further independent literature review is warranted.

value.rationale: An explicitly noted numerical-only trend in a 2024 physical search model is promoted to a rigorous all-parameter theorem, valid for all off-center targets inside a reset interval and a broad natural class of nonincreasing target-distance densities. This provides a mathematically justified reliability design rule: with a dense resetting neighborhood around the target, increasing restart frequency strictly suppresses relative first-passage noise. The monotone-density mixture and signed pair-kernel inequality are nontrivial structural tools beyond routine evaluation of a moment formula. Limits and non-covered classes are explicit.
